question: In the morning, a workshop had 82 items. By afternoon, they removed 37. They removed 30. They tripled. They removed 3. By evening, they multiplied by 7. They removed 227. How many items?
A business had 58 items. Their partner had 120 items. They added 22. They multiplied by 4. They multiplied by 5. They added 35. How many items?
A workshop had 36 items. They added 71. They added 20. They added 74. They removed 148. How many items?
A business had 165 items. There was a dozen distractor items. They doubled. They tripled. They added 3. They multiplied by 6. They removed 1700. How many items?

A workshop had 71 items. They added 70. They removed 39. They divided by 2. There was a distractor of 60 items. They tripled. They added 43. The work took 120 minutes, or 2 hours. They added 64. How many items?

Marcus had 106 dollars in his savings account in the morning. By afternoon, he had quadrupled his money through smart investments. That evening, he gave 46 dollars to his sister Sarah as a gift. The next day, Marcus received 19 dollars in cash from his uncle. He then multiplied his total by 6 when calculating his projected annual savings. Finally, he paid 1253 dollars toward his car loan and received 8 dollars in refund. How much money does Marcus have now?

A bookshop received 68 copies of a new bestseller. The manager doubled the order to prepare for a sale. Then 47 more copies arrived as a bonus shipment. The store multiplied all its stock by 6 to plan for a regional expansion. On opening day, they sold 25 copies to eager customers. The remaining inventory was multiplied by 9 for an online listing. A visiting author had signed 156 books the week before, but that inventory was separate. How many books does the shop now have for sale?

Emma started with 22 beads for her jewelry project. She multiplied her collection by 5 after a shopping trip. Her friend gave her 36 more beads as a gift. Emma then acquired 75 additional beads from a craft fair. She doubled her total collection for safekeeping. Finally, she used 298 beads to make bracelets as gifts. Compared to her friend Sarah, who had half as many beads as Emma started with, how many does Emma have left?

A bakery had 44 loaves at the start of the day. The baker multiplied production by 6 to meet weekend demand. Throughout the morning, customers added 67 loaves to special orders. Another 57 loaves arrived from a partner bakery. Then 35 more custom loaves were requested. Finally, 13 additional loaves came from a delivery. The baker counted 18 loaves reserved for a catering event that were not included in today's total. How many loaves are available after tripling the amount for Monday's planning?

A warehouse started with 71 boxes. They multiplied by 8 when loading shipments. Then by 6 again for a larger truck route. Then by 9 for a full regional distribution center count. After assembly, 8 boxes were damaged and removed. A major loss of 16132 boxes occurred due to a delivery error. Finally, they multiplied the remaining inventory by 9. How many boxes remained in their system for tracking purposes?

A tailor had 49 meters of fabric. They multiplied by 6 when restocking. Then added 67 meters from a supplier. They subtracted 91 meters for large orders. Then subtracted 111 meters for another client project. Finally, subtracted 118 meters for alterations and the remaining stock. Considering that double the original amount would be typical for the season, how much fabric does the tailor have now?

A truck started with 150 packages. In the morning, they added 7 packages. Then removed 118 at the first stop. By afternoon, they added 11 more packages. They removed 43 packages at the second stop. Finally, 6 packages were damaged and removed. Using twice the figure, how many packages does the truck have now?

A supplier had 227 widgets. They added 61 widgets in a shipment. Then 59 more in another delivery. They subtracted 61 widgets that were returned. Finally, 14 widgets were added as replacements. A store owner ordered 350 widgets last month, but this was a separate transaction. What is the final count of widgets in inventory?

A construction site had 146 boxes of supplies. They multiplied by 5 for a major project phase. Then by 9 for the full-scale operation. Then by 6 for multiple team assignments. They subtracted 31756 boxes used in construction. Finally, 3735 more boxes were removed during cleanup. Considering one work crew used these supplies, how much was left?

A printer had 190 reams of paper. They doubled the stock. Then added 19 reams from a new order. They subtracted 385 reams used in printing. Finally, they multiplied by 7 for weekly usage projections. Using the word 'twice', how much paper is in the final projection?

A warehouse started with 113 inventory items. They subtracted 22 items sold. Then removed 34 more damaged items. They removed another 14 items for replacement. Finally, they multiplied the remainder by 5 for regional distribution. Morning and afternoon inventory updates both showed the same changes. How many items are allocated after the afternoon update?

A farm had 228 acres. They doubled the planted area. Then divided by 6 to allocate between crops. They divided by 2 again for separate sections. Then added 60 acres for pasture. Finally, 9 more acres were added for conservation. A neighbor's farm had 300 acres but that was separate. What is the final total?

A manufacturer had 63 units. They doubled production. Then multiplied by 6 for the factory run. They added 8 units from a special order. Finally, they multiplied by 9 for an annual estimate. The quality control team rejected 45 units this month, but those were separate. Accounting for both production changes and inventory, how many units does the manufacturer track?

A storage facility had 206 units. They multiplied by 8 when organizing inventory. Then by 4 for a full account. They added 64 units from new acquisitions. They subtracted 1774 units due to a recall. Finally, 13 units were recovered and added back. Using twice the final count, how many units are in the doubled projection?

A logistics company had 201 shipments. They multiplied by 7 for weekly tracking. Then by 8 for a full network. They divided by 4 to allocate to regions. They multiplied by 4 for multi-day tracking. Finally, they doubled the count for a two-week projection. One warehouse had extra shipments, but those were excluded from this count. How many shipments does the network track?

A library started with 60 reference books. They subtracted 10 old editions. Then added 12 new reference books. They added 35 more from a donation. They subtracted 19 books that needed repair. Finally, 62 books were moved to another location. Between the main library and its satellite branch, how many books are available?

A farm had 56 harvest baskets. They added 46 baskets. Then multiplied by 4 for the full harvest. They subtracted 19 damaged baskets. Finally, they multiplied by 5 and then by 2 for storage planning across two seasons. Using the word 'twice', how many baskets are in the storage projection?

A company had 134 work orders. They multiplied by 3 for a three-month projection. They subtracted 39 orders that were cancelled. Then added 76 new orders. Finally, 50 more orders came in. Tracking these changes along with project milestones, how many orders is the company managing?

A delivery service started with 49 packages. In the morning, they added 7 packages. Then removed 10 packages at a stop. They added 79 packages at the depot. Finally, they multiplied by 6 for a daily load projection. They had a 14-package buffer in reserve that was not included in totals. What is the final package count?

A bakery started with 158 pastries. They added 6 items from a special order. They doubled them for the display. Then added 16 more pastries. Finally, 37 more items arrived. Using the word 'triple', how many pastries does the bakery have after morning production?
